Established 1866

White Oak Pastures is a six generation, 158-year-old family farm in Bluffton, Georgia. We take pride in farming practices that focus on regenerative land management, humane animal husbandry, and revitalizing our rural community. We know radically traditional farming creates products that are better for our land, our livestock and our village. We are fiercely proud of our zero-waste production system that utilizes each part of the animals we pasture-raise and hand-butcher on our farm.

All cattle at White Oak Pastures are grass-fed and grass-finished. Processed in our on-farm, USDA-inspected, zero-waste processing abattoir, our beef never leaves our possession until it's en route to our customers. All of our steaks, roasts, organs, and bones are hand-butchered the old-fashioned way: by a man with a knife.

Our cattle are Certified Grassfed by the American Grassfed Association. All of our livestock are raised without the use of antibiotics, steroids, and added growth hormones.

All of our beef is unaged, unless specifically marked otherwise.

Curious about mRNA in our livestock? Read our statement linked here.

Shipping policy

 

We ship throughout the 48 contiguous states, to any residential address that FedEx and UPS can deliver.

We will only allow a package of perishable product to be in transit for three consecutive days.  Keep in mind that we are shipping from our farm in the Southeast corner of the United States.

We do not recommend shipping to a business address and cannot ship to P.O. boxes.

If your order cannot be received within 3 days using ground shipping, our website will not allow you to choose ground as the shipping option. If you are given the option for ground, it will get there within 3 days of shipping.  If you are not given the ground option, you must use express service. Express service charges are based on weight and distance. If you have any concerns regarding shipping, please contact our office for additional details.

We suggest adding Shipping Protection to your order for peace of mind. For a small fee, you can add this insurance to your order in the event of delays, loss, or theft. Read more about Shipping Protection here. 

For more details, see the Orders & Shipping section of our FAQ page.

White Oak Pastures Shipping FAQs
POSTED BY WHITE OAK PASTURES TEAM
JUN 18, 2022, 3:28:15 PM

Online shopping has become a habit for all of us by now. But while you may not think twice about getting a book shipped to your doorstep, transporting grassfed and pasture-raised meats across the country requires different logistics.

At White Oak Pastures, we ship all of our meats frozen using coolers filled with dry ice. In order for your packages to arrive cold to the touch, we feel that a 3-day ground shipping radius is a comfortable area for us to serve.

If your order contains perishable items, we only have three days to get your order from our warehouse to your doorstep. This reality isn’t an issue for most of our customers, but it does impact shipping options for certain customers (especially those on the west coast). Keep reading to understand why.

Ground Shipping

Ground shipping transports packages through normal trucking channels. Our farm tries to use ground shipping whenever possible, because it is the most cost effective way to get something delivered for most customers.

We offer FREE ground shipping on orders with a product total over $249
We charge $15 ground shipping on orders with a perishable product total over $149
If your product total is under $149, to cover the cost of shipping, we apply a $10 surcharge (more details below)
If your order contains both perishable and non-perishable items, see below for how mixed shipping is charged. 

You are only able to choose ground shipping if  you live within the 3-day shipping zone from White Oak Pastures. If your shipping zone has recently changed, read this blog post to understand why. 

If you live outside of the 3-day ground shipping range, you will need to choose express shipping.

We do not ship to PO Box addresses. View our shipping map here.

Express Shipping

If you do not live within the 2-day ground shipping zone, you cannot choose flat rate ground shipping. 

Orders containing perishable items, shipping outside our 2-day ground network, have to be upgraded to express shipping to speed up transit and fit into the best shipping window. These shipping totals are calculated per pound per mile by our shipping providers, UPS & FedEx.

Since our farm is located in the southeast corner of the United States, if you live on the west coast, it may be likely that you do not live within the 2-day ground shipping zone. We are grateful that you want to support our farm, but at this time we cannot provide ground shipping for your order. 

We do not ship to PO Box addresses. View our shipping map here.

Non-Perishable Shipping

If your order does not contain any perishable items, we have no ground shipping constraints. Orders containing ONLY non-perishables ship via USPS for $15 nationwide.

Mixed Perishable & Non-Perishable Shipping

Orders containing BOTH perishables and non-perishables will ship as follows:

Perishables ship via UPS or FedEx at the rates listed here, depending on location.
Non-perishables will ship via USPS for an additional flat rate of $5.
Cost of shipping will be combined at checkout to display the total rate.
Please note: USPS shipments tend to arrive a few days after UPS/FedEx delivers.
Surcharge for orders under $149

To cover the cost of shipping a cooler, we apply a $10 ground shipping surcharge on orders containing perishable items with a product total of $149 or less.

Many folks find that it is most cost effective to wait to place an order until they have products totaling above $149. It’s a win-win: you get more product, and you save on shipping!

Atlanta Area Courier Delivery

Spend $129 to unlock free courier delivery in select Metro-Atlanta cities. All Courier Delivery orders placed by 12:00 pm EST on a Thursday will be delivered to your designated address the Monday or Tuesday immediately following. By placing your order and selecting the 'Atlanta Courier Delivery' option, you acknowledge that you understand when the next available delivery date will occur.

Your order must include your legal name, phone number, and any additional information such as an apartment number or gate code for access. Refunds and/or reshipment of orders for customers who fail to plan accordingly or decline Shipping Protection will not be permitted. 

Orders arrive in zippered insulated cooler bags with ice packs.

Let us make supporting humane, Regenerative farming easy for you! These convenient meat bundles have been curated to offer a sampler of our grass fed/finished and pasture-raised products.

All of our livestock are raised without the use of antibiotics, steroids, added growth hormones, and mRNA. Curious about mRNA in our livestock? Read our statement linked here.

All cattle at White Oak Pastures are grass-fed and grass-finished. Processed in our on-farm, USDA-inspected, zero-waste processing abattoir, our beef never leaves our possession until it's en route to our customers. All of our steaks, roasts, organs, and bones are hand-butchered the old-fashioned way: by a man with a knife.

Our cattle are Certified Grassfed by the American Grassfed Association.
Our pork is Certified Non-GMO.

Come visit us! You have an open invitation to see first-hand how we do Radically Traditional Farming™ here in Bluffton, Georgia. We believe consumers should know their farmer and have full transparency into the farm to table process. View our on-farm lodging options here.

Butchered in our on-farm processing abattoir, each steak is hand-cut to perfection on our farm. Not every pasture-raised animal is alike, so we take our time butchering piece by piece, step by step. Make your meal a meaningful one with one of our signature cuts.

Our cattle are Certified Grassfed by the American Grassfed Association and all of our livestock are raised without the use of antibiotics, steroids, and added growth hormones.

*Note: We do recommend aging all of our steaks to break down the muscle fibers and create a more tender cut. Visit our blog linked here to learn more about our aging recommendations.
